lesson.title: Der Ausflug zum See
lesson.subtitle: A family trip to a lake: sun, swimming, rain, and a tree

hook.title: Before You Read
hook.content: A Perfekt family story with a simple shape: a good morning, a rainy afternoon, a warm ending. Watch the comparisons — größer als, schöner — and the weather words. The story is about a trip to a lake, not the sea.

footnotes.title: der See / die See
footnotes.content: der See = lake; die See = sea. The article changes the meaning, so the story uses der See and the neuter pronoun pattern around it.

footnotes.title: schwimmen
footnotes.content: schwimmen = to swim. Die Kinder sind im Wasser geschwommen = the children swam in the water. The participle is geschwommen.

pattern.title: Die Geschichte
pattern.content:
Am Wochenende hat Familie Braun einen Ausflug zum See gemacht. Sie sind mit dem Auto gefahren. Der See ist größer als der Fluss in der Stadt.

Das Wetter war schön, und die Sonne schien. Die Kinder sind im Wasser geschwommen. Sie haben viel gelacht.

Am Nachmittag hat es geregnet. Die Familie hat unter einem Baum gewartet. Der Regen war stärker als am Morgen.

Dann sind sie nach Hause gefahren. Der Ausflug war nicht perfekt, aber schön. Die Kinder waren müde und glücklich.

Die Kinder waren stolz und voller Freude. Das Wetter war richtig gut, nicht falsch. Die Decke war sauber, der Korb war leer, und die Tür des Autos war offen. Die Eltern waren nett, die Kinder waren nicht wütend.

exercises.prompt: Reading check — match each story sentence with its English meaning:

matching_pairs.english: The Braun family took a trip to the lake.
matching_pairs.german: Familie Braun hat einen Ausflug zum See gemacht.
Sie sind mit dem Auto gefahren.

matching_pairs.english: The lake is bigger than the river.
matching_pairs.german: Der See ist größer als der Fluss.

matching_pairs.english: The children swam in the water.
matching_pairs.german: Die Kinder sind im Wasser geschwommen.

matching_pairs.english: The family waited under a tree.
matching_pairs.german: Die Familie hat unter einem Baum gewartet.

exercises.target_answer: Familie Braun hat einen Ausflug zum See gemacht., Sie sind mit dem Auto gefahren., Der See ist größer als der Fluss., Die Kinder sind im Wasser geschwommen., Am Nachmittag hat es geregnet., Die Familie hat unter einem Baum gewartet.
exercises.meaning: the trip's sequence: lake, car, swimming, rain, tree, home
exercises.explanation: The six beats are a weather arc: a sunny morning, a swim, a rainy afternoon, shelter, and a warm ending.

exercises.meaning: The family went to a lake.
exercises.explanation: Der Ausflug zum See — zum See means to the lake (der See). The mountain (der Berg) is in the word bank only as a contrast.

exercises.prompt: What did the children do in the water?
exercises.meaning: The children swam in the water.
exercises.explanation: Die Kinder sind im Wasser geschwommen. schwimmen is the verb; geschwommen is its participle.

exercises.prompt: Why did the family wait under a tree?
exercises.meaning: They waited under the tree because it started to rain.
exercises.explanation: Am Nachmittag hat es geregnet. Die Familie hat unter einem Baum gewartet. The rain causes the waiting.

exercises.prompt: Which English follows the German words most closely?
exercises.german: Der See ist größer als der Fluss.
exercises.natural: The lake is bigger than the river.
options: The lake is bigger than the river
The river is bigger than the lake
The lake is as big as the river
The lake is smaller than the river
exercises.target_answer: The lake is bigger than the river
exercises.meaning: The lake is bigger than the river.
exercises.explanation: größer is the comparative of groß; als marks the second item. The river is the smaller one here.

twist.prompt: Without looking back — say in German: 'The lake is bigger than the river.'
twist.target_answer: Der See ist größer als der Fluss
twist.explanation: Comparative + als: Der See ist größer als der Fluss. The mountain (Berg) is a distractor; the comparison is lake versus river.

summary.outcome: Read a Perfekt family-trip story with comparatives and weather words, then answer why and what questions.

use_example.german: Der See ist größer als der Fluss, und am Nachmittag hat es geregnet.
use_example.english: The lake is bigger than the river, and in the afternoon it rained.

summary.takeaway: Weather and comparisons give a trip story its shape: a sunny morning, a rainy afternoon, and a warm conclusion.
summary.curiosity_teaser: You have finished the optional reading library. Re-read any passage for the pleasure of recognising the machinery.

ausflug.context_phrase: Wir machen einen Ausflug in die Berge.
ausflug.context_translation: We take a trip to the mountains.
ausflug.etymology_derivation: aus (out) + Flug (flight, from fliegen — English fly): literally an out-flight, an excursion. [wiktionary]

sonne.etymology_derivation: Old High German sunna — shares Proto-Germanic *sun(n)uz with English sun. [wiktionary]

baum.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *baumaz — English beam is the cognate; a beam was originally a tree. [wiktionary]

familie.etymology_derivation: Borrowed from Latin familia — the same Latin source as English family. [wiktionary]

kind.context_translation: The child plays in the garden.
kind.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *kindą, related to the root of English kin — 'of the family'. The t → z shift never fired here; the d hardened to t instead. [wiktionary]

liebe.context_phrase: Die Liebe ist wichtig im Leben.
liebe.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *lubō — the explicit twin of English love; the noun of lieben. [wiktionary]

nett.etymology_derivation: From Old French net, Latin nitidus — Wiktionary: 'Compare English neat', a shared Romance loan. [wiktionary]

wütend.context_phrase: Er ist wütend auf seinen Bruder.
wütend.context_translation: He is angry at his brother.
wütend.etymology_derivation: wüten (to rage, the Wut family) + -end; no English cognate — memorize this one. [wiktionary]

stolz.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *stultaz 'proud, stiff' — English stout is the named cognate. [wiktionary]

freude.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *frawiþō, from the 'jump for joy' root; only Dutch cognates named — see Schadenfreude. [wiktionary]

richtig.etymology_derivation: recht (right, the gh→ch twin) + -ig — 'right-y', the same root as English right. [wiktionary]

falsch.etymology_derivation: Proto-West Germanic *falskī, from Latin falsus — the same Latin line as English false. [wiktionary]

sauber.etymology_derivation: Ultimately from Latin sobrius — the same Latin word behind English sober. [wiktionary]

leer.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *lēziz — English leer is the listed cognate, both originally 'empty'. [wiktionary]

offen.etymology_derivation: Proto-West Germanic *opan — English open is listed among cognates, kin to auf. [wiktionary]

see.etymology_derivation: From Old High German sē, from Proto-West Germanic *saiwi, from Proto-Germanic *saiwiz. English sea is the listed cognate; der See is the lake, die See the sea. [wiktionary]

fluss.context_phrase: Der Fluss fließt durch die Stadt.
fluss.context_translation: The river flows through the city.
fluss.etymology_derivation: From Middle High German vluȥ, from Proto-Germanic *flutiz, from the same root as fließen, to flow. English flow is the cognate of that root. [wiktionary]

berg.context_phrase: Der Berg ist im Winter weiß.
berg.context_translation: The mountain is white in winter.
berg.etymology_derivation: From Old High German bërg, from Proto-West Germanic *berg, from Proto-Germanic *bergaz. English barrow, a burial hill, is the listed cognate. [wiktionary]

auto.etymology_derivation: Short for Automobil — the same Greek autos ('self') loan as English auto, clipped German-style. [wiktionary]

wochenende.context_phrase: Am Wochenende fahren wir an den See.
wochenende.context_translation: On the weekend we go to the lake.
wochenende.etymology_derivation: Woche + Ende — the modern compound arose in the 19th century as a calque of English weekend; Woche is the twin of week (k → ch) and Ende the twin of end. [wiktionary]

schön.etymology_derivation: Proto-Germanic *skauniz — the twin of archaic English sheen 'beautiful'. [wiktionary]

müde.context_phrase: Ich bin müde und gehe ins Bett.
müde.context_translation: I am tired and go to bed.
müde.etymology_derivation: Proto-West Germanic *mōþī; only Dutch moe named — no English cognate, memorize this one. [wiktionary]
